audit_items.proof_trace: `util_rate = debt / (debt + cash - cash_reserve)` exceeds 1 whenever `cash < cash_reserve`. `accrue_interest` (L125-149) grows `cash_reserve` by `reserve_factor * interest_accumulated` without any guard that `cash >= cash_reserve` remains satisfied, while `cash` is unchanged. At near-100% utilization a sustained period without repayment causes `cash_reserve > cash`, breaking the invariant. The downstream `calc_interest` (interest.move:85-96) then computes `weight = (util_rate - high_kink) / (1 - high_kink) > 1`, yielding interest rates above `max_borrow_rate` and accelerating the reserve accumulation on each subsequent accrual.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A market at ~99.9% utilization (cash=1, debt=999) accumulates protocol reserves over time via unchecked `accrue_interest` calls (triggered by any market interaction); once `cash_reserve > cash`, `util_rate > 1`, the interest model enters a runaway regime computing rates above the configured ceiling, compounding interest faster than borrowers can repay and eroding lender funds through excess reserve capture.
